# Template: size_compare
Two to four things drawn TO THE SAME SCALE so their sizes can be compared by eye: planets as discs, countries as squares of their area, lengths as bars, animals or objects as icons — each with its name and value, and the ratio between the biggest and the smallest written once ("109 × as wide", "14 × the area", "1.3 million × the volume"). `measure` says how a value becomes a drawn size: diameter or length linearly, area by its square root, volume or mass by its cube root (same density). `layout`: beside (on one baseline), row (on one centre line), inside (the small ones drawn inside the big one, labels in a column beside it) or overlay (all centred on one point). `count_fit: true` fills a row with copies of one item — across the big one (109 Earths across the Sun), or across a `gap` (30 Earths between the Earth and the Moon). A thing too small to see at that scale is drawn as a dot with a ring and its label, never enlarged; a `camera` beat (`camera: {center: {ref: "<item>_shape"}, zoom: 8}`) zooms to it. Choose this scene for ANY "how big is X next to Y", "as big as", "would fit inside", "how many X fit in Y", "drawn to scale" or "the true size of" request — planets, countries, animals, organs, buildings, storage media.

Element ids your commands can reference:
- <item>_shape: the item drawn to scale (a group) — earth_shape, africa_shape; a choose option ("which is bigger? tap it")
- <item>_label: its name and value (a ring or a leader line to a tiny one comes with it)
- ratio: the ratio between the biggest and the smallest, written once ("109 × as wide")
- fit_row: with count_fit, the row of copies (one group; draw it on its own beat)
- fit_label: with count_fit, how many fit ("30 × Earth")
- gap_line: with gap, the dimension line between the first two centres (its gap_label comes with it)
- gap_label: with gap, the distance written over it
- shapes: every item's shape (a name for the set)
- labels: every item's label (a name for the set)
Examples:
Request: "How many Earths would fit across the Sun?" → params: {"measure":"diameter","layout":"inside","count_fit":true,"items":[{"name":"Sun","value":1391400,"unit":"km","color":"#f2c14e"},{"name":"Earth","value":12742,"unit":"km","color":"#2f6b8f"}]}
Request: "How big is Greenland really, compared with Africa?" → params: {"measure":"area","layout":"inside","items":[{"name":"Africa","value":30.37,"unit":"million km²","color":"#d0865f"},{"name":"Greenland","value":2.17,"unit":"million km²","color":"#2f6b8f"}]}
Request: "How many Earths fit between the Earth and the Moon?" → params: {"measure":"diameter","layout":"row","gap":{"value":384400,"label":"384,400 km"},"count_fit":true,"items":[{"name":"Earth","value":12742,"unit":"km","color":"#2f6b8f"},{"name":"Moon","value":3474,"unit":"km","color":"#8f887c"}]}

In YAML: `template: size_compare` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
